The above analysis was repeated for a fixed A’ = 2.5 m2/m3 across multiple locations in California, carbon emission price scenarios and soar multiples. Trona, Coalinga, Lost Hills, San Ardo and Stockton with annual average DNI values spanning from 8.1 to 6.6 kWh/m2-day were considered for the analysis. Figure 54 presents contour maps of the minimum LCOH and the corresponding optimal storage capacity for solar multiples of 2 and 3. The contours are presented as a function of the carbon emission prices and the annual average DNI obtained by linearly interpolating results computed for the five locations analyzed in this study. The optimal TES capacity increases with increase in solar field size, as represented by the solar multiple. For a 45 MW IPH demand and a solar multiple of 3, the optimal storage capacity ranges between 575 and 685 MWh, which is approximately 13 to 15 hours of effective storage. For a solar multiple of 2, the optimal Page 79 of 87 DE-EE0009329 Element 16 Technologies, Inc. TES capacity ranges between 165 and 250 MWh, equivalent to 3.5 to 5.5 hours of effective storage duration. As expected, the minimum LCOH decreases with increase in carbon emission price, and the corresponding optimal TES capacity increases due to the stronger economic incentive to displace natural gas use for IPH. At solar multiple of 3.0, the LCOH of the hybrid solar+TES+backup boiler system is lower than that of a stand- alone natural gas boiler (3.8 cents/kWh) even when carbon pricing is not considered, provided the annual average DNI of the location exceeds 6.9 kWh/m2/day. As seen from Figure 54c, for locations with annual average DNI below 6.9 kWh/m2/day, the hybrid system achieves a lower LCOH than stand-alone natural gas boiler only for carbon emission prices above 5 $/ton. However, at low annual average DNI, a smaller solar field integrated with sulfur TES of lower capacity yields a lower LCOH than stand-alone natural gas boiler (Figure 54a). Overall, this integrated modeling framework enables Element 16 to conduct location-specific annual simulations and technoeconomic analysis to identify the optimal configuration for various industrial process heat application requirements and market conditions.
